findings.explanation: The Facebook webhook GET verification handshake compares the caller-supplied hub.verify_token to the configured fbVerifyToken using strict equality (===) instead of crypto.timingSafeEqual. This is a non-constant-time comparison of a secret value, unlike the POST handler's HMAC check on the same file (verifySignature, line 265-280) which correctly uses crypto.timingSafeEqual. Character-by-character timing differences could theoretically let a remote attacker brute-force fbVerifyToken faster than guessing blind, though network jitter makes exploitation harder in practice and the token alone does not grant access to send/forge webhook events (POST payloads are separately authenticated via HMAC signature). Fix: hash both sides (or pad to equal length) and use crypto.timingSafeEqual, consistent with the safeEqualSecret/safeEqualText helpers already used elsewhere in admin-auth.js and admin/session.js.
